successors.note: Cliopatria runs the shape to 1768; the page dates the annexation to 1766.

capitals.name: Nancy
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Nancy' with no years. Nancy is held by the duke in 1475-1476 (René II page). Stanisław lived at a country estate in Lunéville and Leopold 'continued to reign at the Château de Lunéville'; the gazetteer's Nancy is 6.20 E, 48.68 N.

keyframe_review.note: 17.4 k km2 for 1431-1439: Lorraine with Bar (the 1431 outline reaches 4.9 E; the 1453 outline of Lorraine alone starts at 5.9 E). Bar page: 'In 1430, the last duke of the male line of the ruling house, Louis, died. Bar passed to his great-nephew, René I, who was married to Isabella, Duchess of Lorraine. In 1431 the couple inherited Lorraine.' Neither the Lorraine nor the Bar infobox gives an area, so no ratio can be taken.

10.3 k km2: Lorraine without Bar. The Bar page says Bar was 'united to the imperial Duchy of Lorraine' only 'from 1480', so the pair stand apart in 1453-1479. The pages opened do not date the separation in 1453 (ledger event at confidence 1). No infobox area.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Lorraine shape in 1440-1452 and draws the land inside House of Valois-Anjou (43 of 44 cells in 1445), the shape of René of Anjou's lands. The Bulgnéville page shows Lorraine continuing as René's duchy: 'Sigismund declared against Vaudémont at an arbitration court in Basel in 1434, awarding Lorraine to René', and the 1444-1445 marriages 'gave additional stability to the peace'. The 1431 outline (Lorraine with Bar) is kept. The house-of-valois-anjou dossier should drop these cells.

correction.text: Lorraine with Bar under René of Anjou, awarded the duchy by Sigismund at Basel in 1434

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no shape for 1475-1481 and draws the land inside the Duchy of Burgundy (42 of 44 cells in 1478). The René II page keeps the duchy as René's: Charles the Bold 'invaded the duchy and René was forced to quit Nancy (30 November 1475)', René 'regained the city on 5 October the following year', and won 'the Battle of Nancy (5 January 1477)'. The 1474 outline of Lorraine alone is kept; the occupation of 1475-1476 is hatched by the ledger.

The pages opened show the duchy in being: the Treaty of Vienna (signed 18 November 1738) gave 'the duchies of Lorraine and Bar' to Stanisław, 'to pass to his daughter' (the wife of Louis XV) on his death; Stanisław's infobox reign is 9 July 1737 to 23 February 1766. French administration, and any occupation in 1734-1736, are not on the pages opened.

Stanisław Leszczyński was Duke of Lorraine and Bar throughout ('Reign: 9 July 1737 – 23 February 1766'; 'lived out his remaining years at a country estate in Lunéville'), so the 1756 outline is kept.

region.text: Lorraine with Bar, inherited by René of Anjou and Isabella

ledger.note: 1431: Duke Charles II dies and René of Anjou, husband of his daughter Isabella, inherits Lorraine and Bar. 'After Charles' death in January 1431, Antoine renewed his fight for the duchy'; Bar page: 'In 1431 the couple inherited Lorraine.' The duchy itself is older (959-965, Duchy page) and Cliopatria's row starts here; the page gives the cities, not a boundary, so the region is Cliopatria's 1431 outline.

region.text: Bar: the 1487 outline of Lorraine with Bar minus the 1453 outline of Lorraine alone

ledger.note: 1453: Bar parts from Lorraine in Cliopatria's shapes. Page silent on the year: the Bar page says Bar passed to René I and was 'united to the imperial Duchy of Lorraine' only from 1480, so for 1453-1479 Bar is René of Anjou's own; the year is bridged from the change of shape.

1473: René II succeeds his cousin as Duke of Lorraine. 'Reign: 24 July 1473 – 10 December 1508'; the Duchy page: 'ruled by the dukes of the House of Lorraine after 1473' (the Vaudémont line replaces the Angevin line; colour and dossier continue).

region.text: the duchy of Lorraine invaded by Charles the Bold, René forced to quit Nancy

ledger.note: 1475: Charles the Bold of Burgundy occupies Lorraine and drives René II out of Nancy. 'Charles invaded the duchy and René was forced to quit Nancy (30 November 1475).'

region.text: the duchy of Lorraine, Nancy regained by René II

ledger.note: 1476: René II retakes Nancy. 'He regained the city on 5 October the following year.' The Battle of Nancy page has Charles besieging the city from 22 October 1476 and René winning 'the Battle of Nancy (5 January 1477)'; the Burgundian hold on Lorraine ends for good there.

region.text: Bar: the 1487 outline of Lorraine with Bar minus the 1453 outline of Lorraine alone

ledger.note: 1480: Bar passes to René II and is united with Lorraine. 'On René's death in 1480, Bar passed to his daughter Yolanda and her son, René II, who was already Duke of Lorraine'; 'From 1480, it was united to the imperial Duchy of Lorraine.' Cliopatria starts the union in 1487.

region.text: the prévôté of Virton, a part of the Duchy of Luxembourg

ledger.note: 1482: René II conquers the prévôté of Virton and annexes it to Bar. 'In 1482 he conquered the prévôté of Virton, a part of the Duchy of Luxembourg, and annexed it to Bar.' The region is a 12 km circle about Virton at 5.53 E, 49.57 N because the gazetteer lacks the name; Virton lies outside Cliopatria's Lorraine outlines, and in 1482 the Duchy of Luxembourg was a Habsburg land (Duchy of Luxembourg page: infobox 'To Habsburg: 1482'; 'The Burgundian Netherlands then came under the rule of the House of Habsburg'), so the counterpart is house-of-habsburg, whose 1482 gain takes the Burgundian Netherlands; the duchy-of-luxembourg dossier ends in 1443. Counterpart corrected by the eu-09-h reviewer.

region.text: the duchy of Lorraine invaded by French troops

ledger.note: 1633: French troops invade Lorraine. 'in 1633, French troops invaded' in retaliation for Charles IV's support of Gaston d'Orléans; the Duchy page dates the occupation to 1634: 'France was able to occupy the duchy in 1634 and retained it until 1661 when Charles IV was restored.' Charles abdicated in January 1634 (infobox).

region.text: the duchy of Lorraine, restored to Charles IV

ledger.note: 1661: the French withdraw and Charles IV returns. 'In 1661, the French withdrew from Lorraine'; Duchy page: 'retained it until 1661 when Charles IV was restored'. The Treaty of Vincennes page did not load, so the terms (land ceded to France) are not entered.

region.text: the duchy of Lorraine occupied by France

ledger.note: 1670: France occupies Lorraine again and Charles IV goes into exile. 'In 1670, the duchy was again occupied by the French under King [Louis XIV]'; Duchy page: 'In 1670, the French invaded again, forcing Charles into exile'.

region.text: the duchy of Lorraine, returned at Ryswick

ledger.note: 1697: the Treaty of Ryswick returns Lorraine. The treaty 'returned other territories occupied or captured since then' and the Duchy of Lorraine 'to the Holy Roman Empire' (negotiations 20 September to 30 October 1697); Duchy page: 'France returned the Duchy in the 1697 Treaty of Ryswick'. The page does not say when Leopold entered the duchy, and Cliopatria's shape returns in 1700.

region.text: parts of Lorraine, including the capital Nancy, occupied by France

ledger.note: 1702: France occupies parts of Lorraine again. 'in the 1701–1714 War of the Spanish Succession, parts of Lorraine, including the capital Nancy, were again occupied by France'; infobox 'French invasion during War of the Spanish Succession: 1702'. The page names parts, not their extent, so the whole outline is hatched as Cliopatria draws it.
1713: the French occupation ends. Page silent on the withdrawal: it gives the war as 1701-1714; the year is bridged from Cliopatria's shape returning in 1713.

1737: Stanisław Leszczyński becomes Duke of Lorraine and Bar. Infobox 'Reign: 9 July 1737 – 23 February 1766'; Duchy page: 'the Lorraine House of Vaudémont assigned the Duchy to Stanisław Leszczyński' after the War of the Polish Succession; Francis Stephen is indemnified with Tuscany (Treaty of Vienna, signed 18 November 1738). Colour and dossier continue.

region.text: Lorraine with Bar, annexed by France

ledger.note: 1766: Stanisław dies and France annexes Lorraine. 'When Stanisław died on 23 February 1766, Lorraine was annexed by France' (infobox 'Annexed by France: 1766'); Stanisław page: the duchies 'were to revert to France on his death'.

wars.name: War of the Lorraine Succession
wars.outcome: Antoine de Vaudémont won the Battle of Bulgnéville (2 July 1431) and René of Anjou was captured and handed to the Duke of Burgundy; Sigismund awarded Lorraine to René at Basel in 1434; the marriage of René's daughter Yolande to Antoine's son Frederick, 'only fulfilled in 1445', settled the peace.
wars.note: The Wikipedia article 'War of the Lorraine Succession' did not load; the Bulgnéville page does not record any ground held by Antoine, so no contest event is entered.

wars.name: Burgundian Wars (Lorraine campaign)

zones.text: Lorraine invaded by Charles the Bold, Nancy lost on 30 November 1475

wars.outcome: René II recovered Nancy (5 October 1476) and 'defeated and killed Charles at the Battle of Nancy (5 January 1477)'.

wars.name: French occupation of Lorraine (1633-1661)
wars.outcome: France invaded in 1633, 'was able to occupy the duchy in 1634 and retained it until 1661 when Charles IV was restored'.
wars.note: Wikipedia's war and treaty pages for these years (Franco-Spanish War, Peace of the Pyrenees, Treaty of Vincennes) were not opened or did not load.

wars.name: French occupation of Lorraine (1670-1697), ended by the Treaty of Ryswick
wars.outcome: France invaded in 1670 and Charles IV went into exile; the 1697 Treaty of Ryswick returned the Duchy of Lorraine.
wars.note: The Ryswick page names the duchy only in passing; the 1670 invasion is on the Charles IV and Duchy pages.

wars.name: War of the Spanish Succession (Lorraine)

zones.text: parts of Lorraine, including the capital Nancy

wars.outcome: 'parts of Lorraine, including the capital Nancy, were again occupied by France'; the page does not date the withdrawal.

wars.name: Settlement of the War of the Polish Succession (Lorraine and Bar)
wars.outcome: Stanisław Leszczyński received the duchies of Lorraine and Bar for his lifetime, to pass to Louis XV's wife on his death; Francis Stephen was indemnified with Tuscany (Treaty of Vienna, signed 18 November 1738).
wars.note: The years of the war itself are not on the pages opened; this entry covers only the settlement that moved Lorraine.

certainty.note: No treaty line or survey is dated on the pages opened; the outlines are Cliopatria's. Bar's frontier was split between the Empire and France ('Barrois mouvant' a French fief from 1301, Bar page) and the enclaves of the Three Bishoprics are not drawn.

notes: Cliopatria's row 1431-1768 is read as one state, the Duchy of Lorraine (founded 959-965 per the Duchy page), with Bar added in two phases: 1431-1452 (René of Anjou, Lorraine with Bar), 1453-1479 (Lorraine alone) and 1480-1766 (the two united under René II and his successors). Start 1431 is Cliopatria's first year; the duchy's earlier life (959-1430) is not reviewed. The page budget was spent on nine pages. Pages that did not load: War of the Lorraine Succession and Treaty of Vincennes (1661). Cliopatria gaps (1440-1452, 1475-1481, 1636-1647, 1673-1699, 1702-1712, 1734-1747, 1757-1762) are filled by new keyframes using the neighbouring outline: in the gaps the land is drawn as House of Valois-Anjou (1440-1452), Duchy of Burgundy (1475-1481) and Kingdom of France (the rest), so those dossiers need to drop the cells. Not entered for lack of a page: the Three Bishoprics (Metz, Toul, Verdun) taken by France in 1552; the terms of the Treaty of Vincennes of 1661; the date Leopold entered the duchy after Ryswick; the end of the 1702 occupation; any French occupation of 1733-1737; the Guise inheritance of 1504 (a French fief, outside the outline); the Lorraine and Bar areas (no infobox gives one). The Cliopatria shape changes after 1487 are 1-4 cells each, which this dossier reads as cell noise. Bar is not a Cliopatria row: the Bar region is taken as the difference of two Lorraine outlines. A gap-filler should open Isabella of Lorraine / John II of Lorraine (1453), the Peace of the Pyrenees and Treaty of Vincennes (1659-1661) and the War of the Polish Succession.
